pageCache.pageTitle: Year 3 & 4: Exploring Science, Geography and Storytelling - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Year 3 & 4: Exploring Science, Geography and Storytelling
This week Year 3 have started their unit in Science all about the musculoskeletal system. In D&T this week we have explored the best bag for fossils, and we have spoken about the materials that we might need to make it. In Maths, we will be learning about fractions and some children have been looking at how we might half and quarter real objects like bread.
This week in Year 4, the children continued their learning about mountains and volcanos. This week they thought about the environmental and human impacts of mountains – both positives and negatives. In Science, the children refreshed their understanding of the states of matter including the scientific definition of each in relation to volume and shape. The children began creating their story maps for the new model text, Bed Monsters, with lots of fun actions and colourful drawings.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception: Sunshine, Stories and Science - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception: Sunshine, Stories and Science
We have had a great few days in Nursery this week making the most of the sunny weather. We have enjoyed watching bubbles in the sun and trying to catch them. In Talk for Writing, we have been learning the Cave Baby story map and learning our story vocabulary. World Book Day was fantastic - we enjoyed coming to school as different good and evil characters and we enjoyed books and stories as well as our first whole school assembly where we played the TLAP Masked Reader!
This week, Reception carried out an exciting experiment to explore how moon craters are formed. The children dropped different objects into flour to represent meteors hitting the moon’s surface and observed the craters that were created. We talked about how rocks from space crash into the moon and leave marks behind. The children loved making predictions and observing the different crater shapes and sizes.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Growing Independence and Sunflower Smiles in Early Years - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Growing Independence and Sunflower Smiles in Early Years
This week, we have started our last half term in Nursery. Our week has started with a new class text, Sunflower Sisters by Monika Singh Gangotra. We have planted our own sunflower each, which we will watch grow in the next few weeks. We have been making sunflowers and creating a sunflower wall in the nursery! We are busy gardening, learning all about plants and how they grow. We are also working hard to be as independent as possible, ready for September.
This week in Reception, we have started reading the story Julian is a Mermaid. We have been making predictions about what might happen next in the story and discussing why Julian says, “Uh oh” halfway through the book. The children shared some wonderful ideas and used clues from the story to support their predictions. In Maths, we have been learning about sharing. We explored different ways to share resources equally between groups and discussed what makes sharing fair. The children enjoyed using practical resources to help them understand this important concept.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 1 & 2: Giants and Superheroes Inspire Creative Learning - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Year 1 & 2: Giants and Superheroes Inspire Creative Learning
On Monday, the children in Year 1 returned to school to find out that a friendly tree giant had been spotted in the playground over half term. The children came up with a whole set of adjectives and similes to describe the tree giant. They then drew their own tree giants. Over the next few weeks, they are going to be learning how to write information texts using the tree giant as an example.
Year 2 have had an exciting start to the term as they stepped into the world of superheroes, designing their very own unique characters and putting their creative skills to the test in T4W. The children have shown incredible imagination and enthusiasm. They then carried this creativity into science, where they explored different habitats and thought carefully about what environments their superheroes would need to survive and thrive.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 3 & 4: Science, Stories and Spring Poetry - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Year 3 & 4: Science, Stories and Spring Poetry
This week, Year 3 have been having fun exploring spring poetry for the upcoming spring concert. In Science, they have been setting up experiments to see the skeletons function and test their theories. In D&T they have been working really hard practising different stitches in preparation for making their fossil bags at the end of the term.
This week in Year 4, the children continued learning our new story map – a non-fiction text about a fiction creature. In Science, the children continued learning about the behaviour of atoms in the different states of matter. They enjoyed seeing this using an online simulation. In History, the children compared the burial traditions of ancient Egypt and Rome. On Thursday, we enjoyed several different activities for World Book Day, including a workshop by Word on the Street.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 1 & 2: Maths, Maps and Meals - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Year 1 & 2: Maths, Maps and Meals
This week, Year 1 continued their leaning in Fractions, exploring more about quarters and halves. We have also started innovating our text map in T4W, writing our own texts about the character of our choice. In Science we have been sorting out objects into groups according to the material they are made of.
This week, the children had a fantastic time creating their own vegetable kebabs, carefully practising their cutting skills and learning how to handle tools safely and confidently. They explored a colourful range of vegetables, discussing textures, flavours, and the importance of healthy eating as they assembled their creations. In Geography, the class began investigating coastal towns, using Lyme Regis as a case study to understand what makes these locations unique. They focused on key features such as local landmarks and how the town has adapted to its seaside environment.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Reception 2026 Starters - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Reception 2026 Starters
Starting Reception is an exciting milestone for children and their families. With National Offer Day taking place in April, many parents begin thinking about the transition to school and how best to support their child for this important next step.
This page is designed to help parents so that children are ready to start school in the best way possible.
Starting Reception
To help make the transition into Reception as smooth and positive as possible, we encourage you to explore Starting Reception (www.startingreception.co.uk), where you’ll find practical tips, activities and guidance to help your child feel confident on their first day. Supporting your child now can make a big difference in helping them thrive in September.
Potty Training
As your child prepares to start Reception, we encourage families to continue supporting them in developing independence with toileting, as this is one of the skills that helps children feel confident and settled in school (unless there is a diagnosed medical condition, such as a bowel or bladder condition). You may find our Potty Training Guide helpful, which has been developed in line with guidance from early years experts, and of course please do get in touch if you would like to discuss your child’s individual needs.
Children's Toothbrushing
Please click on the link below to view a very useful guide on children's tooth brushing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception: Imagination Takes Flight - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception: Imagination Takes Flight
Nursery have come back to another busy week. We have started reading our new class text, 'Cave Baby' by Julia Donaldson about a baby who uses his imagination to paint pre-historic animals on cave walls. We have been exploring imagination and what it means to imagine. We have been practising our independence again and making sure we have a try at doing something before we ask for help.
This week the children have settled back into the school routine wonderfully and we have had another amazing week. To celebrate Pancake Day, the children enjoyed making (and tasting) their very own pancakes, carefully following instructions and working as a team. The children came in on Tuesday to see that one of our classrooms had been transformed into outer space! We had lots of fun exploring our new classroom environment and pretending that we were real astronauts. We also continued learning about important celebrations, including Ramadan, Lent and Lunar New Year, exploring different cultures and traditions.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception: A Week of Imagination, Growing and Planting - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception: A Week of Imagination, Growing and Planting
Nursery had another busy week this week. We have started reading our new class text, 'Harold and the Purple Crayon' by Crocket Johnson. The book is about a boy who uses his imagination, alongside a purple crayon to draw an imagined world. We have been exploring imagination and what it means to imagine. We have also enjoyed watching our 4 ducklings grow bigger and bigger. We have given them baths, watched them splash in puddles and given them cuddles. We have said goodbye to them as they journey back to their farm today to live with their brothers and sisters!
This week, Reception have been busy exploring planting as part of both our Talk for Writing and Science learning. The children have enjoyed writing instructions for Miss LaTour, helping her to learn how to plant flowers carefully and successfully. In Maths, we have been focusing on 3D shapes, identifying and describing their properties. We are also very excited to be celebrating Comic Relief this week and taking part in the fun activities together
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 3 & 4: Faith, Food and Fantastic Experiences - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Year 3 & 4: Faith, Food and Fantastic Experiences
This week, Year 3 were fortunate to have a visit from a Rabi to support their learning of Judaism. They learned all about Passover and what Jewish people eat during that time. They got the opportunity to taste traditional foods like unleavened Matzah (unleavened bread).
This week in Year 4, the children have participated in two investigations about reversible changes of state. For freezing, the children made ice cream and melted different food products in our hands. In RE, the children learned about the events to Holy Week and its significance to Christians. They had a wonderful time at Ufton Court enhancing their learning on the ancient Romans.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception: Storytelling, Sunshine and Springtime Creations - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception: Storytelling, Sunshine and Springtime Creations
This week in NJursery we have been learning our new story map, making sure we are using fantastic story telling voices to make the story exciting to listen to. We have also been learning the actions to bring our story to life. We have been enjoying the sun, playing in the reception garden, building mud pies and splashing in water.
This week, the children in Reception designed creative costumes for Mrs Bowen, showing fantastic imagination and enthusiasm. In Talk for Writing, we created a story map based on Greta Thunberg’s biography, helping the children to sequence events and build their storytelling skills. In Maths, we explored tally charts and revisited the concepts of one more and one less to strengthen our number understanding. In Topic, we got creative by making beautiful tulips using PVA glue, soap, and paint—be sure to take a look at them displayed on our classroom windows!
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

Year 1 & 2: Inventors, Arrays and Exploring China
On Wednesday, Year 1 celebrated Shanker Bhise’ birthday. They learned about his inventions and enjoyed participating in a variety of activities like, potato and sponge printing, making paper cup telephones, weighing and balancing groceries and objects.
Year 2 have been learning how to use arrays to solve multiplication and division reasoning problems, showing great progress in using visual strategies to explain their thinking. They have also begun exploring China, gathering key facts to create a case study and learning what makes the country unique. In Science, the class created healthy-living leaflets, explaining the importance of good sleep, a balanced diet and regular exercise to help us stay well.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.text:
Local Newspaper Coverage
We are excited to share that we feature in the “Preserving the Past, Shaping the Future: The Vital Role of Heritage in Education” series in our local newspapers (Slough Observer and Bucks Free Press). We are proud to have been recognised among the “most distinguished schools in our community” and counted as one of the “community’s finest educational institutions”. The article highlights how a strong sense of heritage shapes not only a school’s identity but also its values, resilience and approach to education, creating a “living legacy” that connects past, present and future generations. It celebrates institutions that successfully balance tradition with innovation, fostering belonging, inspiring achievement and ensuring students see themselves as active participants in an enduring story of learning and community impact. Please take a moment to read the article when you have a chance, it’s a great reminder that we should all be proud of who we are.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Making Every Moment Count in Years 3 and 4 - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Making Every Moment Count in Years 3 and 4
This week, Year 3 have continued their work in maths on time, understanding and calculating durations of time. Billinghurst celebrated Rosa Billinghurst’s birthday, learning about gender and equality and rights to vote. They designed rosettes and posters and performed a peaceful protest in the classroom.
This week, Year 4 have been working exceptionally hard to improve their times tables recall. We are certain the children will make us, you and them proud of their commitment to learning all their times tables! We have also researched food from around the world. Year 4 discussed the prices, nutritional values and compared them to other food! This links to our new Talk4Writing unit- where we are discussing the inspirational work of Marcus Rashford.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery & Reception: Sunflowers, Mermaids and Medical Marvels - Latest News - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Nursery & Reception: Sunflowers, Mermaids and Medical Marvels
This week in Nursery, the children have been working hard to learn their new story map, Sunflower Sisters. We have been using our voices, changing the tone and emphasis of different words to make the story exciting. We have also enjoyed getting messy with foam and painting lots of sunflowers for our sunflower wall.
This week in Reception we have started learning our new Talk for Writing story Julian is a Mermaid and the children have really enjoyed taking part in a range of activities linked to the story, showing wonderful enthusiasm and creativity. We also had a visit from a very special visitor – a nurse! The children learned all about how nurses help us, including how to wash our hands properly, apply bandages and even use some of the equipment found in hospitals. The children loved having the opportunity to see real medical equipment and they asked some fantastic questions. In Maths, we have been exploring odd and even numbers in a range of contexts. We have also continued practising for Sports Day, which everyone is very excited for. It has been another fantastic week, and we are so proud of the children’s enthusiasm and hard work.
Headteacher - Mrs T Bowen

pageCache.pageTitle: Class Pages - The Langley Academy Primary
pageCache.text:
Class Pages
As the school grows year groups will be referred to by a given attribute. Throughout the year children will learn more about the person that their class is named after.
Nursery
Nursery are our youngest pupils, therefore they are referred to as ‘Pioneers’.
Morning Nursery is named Edwards: After Tracy Edwards MBE, who in 1989, skippered the first all-female crew in the Whitbread Round the World Yacht Race. Finishing second, they hold the record for the best result since 1977, the best ever result for an all-female crew and she was the first woman to be awarded Yachtsman of the Year.
Afternoon Nursery is named Peake: After Tim Peake, the first British astronaut to go on board the International Space Station, bearing a British flag patch. He is the first British person to fly into space without a private contract or foreign citizenship and the first Brit to participate in a spacewalk outside the International Space Station (ISS). He was the first man to run the London Marathon from ISS treadmill.
Reception
We want our Reception children to be confident in their explorations. Therefore, their classes are named after explorers.
Sue Hendrickson is a self-taught fossil hunter, marine archaeologist, adventurer and explorer. In 1990, she found the largest and most complete T-Rex to date. She has also found important fossils, artefacts and shipwrecks around the world.
Amelia Earhart was the first lady to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean. During World War 1, Amelia became interested in caring for wounded soldiers. In 1920, she went on her first aeroplane ride. That encouraged her to take flying lessons. Soon afterwards she bought her first plane and gained her pilot’s license. Whilst working as a social worker, she continued her interest in aviation. In 1928, she was selected to fly across the Atlantic as a passenger. In 1928, she flew across the Atlantic alone. She completed many flights in the years that followed.
Junk Tabei was a Japanese mountaineer, author and teacher. She was the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest. As part of a Japanese Woman’s climbing group, they applied for licences to climb Everest. It took years before it was approved! The trip had many challenges but on 16 May 1975 Tabei succeeded. She also climbed the highest peak of mountains in each continent. In total, Tabei climbed around 70 mountains. She has an asteroid named after her.
Year 1
In Year 1, we want the children to explore their understanding further through innovation. Therefore, our Year 1 classes are named after inventors.
Grace Hopper was an American computer scientist who led the development of COBOL – a high-level computing programming language. In 1928, she graduated in mathematics and physics. She developed a working computer, then went on to develop COBOL: In the 1950s a language that resembles English language rather than code. COBOL is still in use today.
Philip Downing was a black, American inventor. He invented many things but is especially famous for what Americans call the ‘mailbox’ (and we refer to as a post-box). His invention meant that people did not have to walk to the post office with letters to be sent. He invented the mailbox in 1891. He also worked as a postal clerk so was able to use this knowledge to identify needs and create something to make life easier.
Shankar Bhise was an Indian inventor. As a young child, he was interested in reading scientific magazines and this inspired him to learn more about mechanical engineering. In 1890 he won a competition to design an machine for weighing groceries, this helped him travel to London so that he could get investment to make his inventions. He invented an electronic signboard, an automatic flushing toilet, a telephone and several items for the kitchen.
Year 2
Much of the Year 2 curriculum focusses on the seven seas. Therefore, the classes are named after a variety of travellers. We want the children to feel compelled to find out more about the world around them.
Ramnath Biswas was born in India in 1894. He is famous for travelling around the globe by bicycle. One of his first jobs was working as a mechanic, during this role he learned how to drive and ride a bicycle. During World War 1, he worked with the British Navy. He travelled the world between 1931 and 1940. He self-published a book about his travels.
In 2019, Jessica Nabongo became the first black woman to document travelling every country in the world. She has many talents and is a writer, photographer, travel expert and business woman. When Nabongo was 6 years old she travelled to London. That became her inspiration, she daydreamed of visiting foreign lands. Jessica has made this dream a reality and shares her travel experiences in her book and blogs.
Jacques Cousteau was a French naval officer, oceanographer, filmmaker and author. In the 1940s he had the dream of sharing inaccessible places to the world. He made his first underwater film. He enjoyed deep sea diving and was very frustrated that he could not spend enough time underwater. He improved the equipment he had and developed a system to support scuba diving. This helped further his work, which included travelling the seas to create underwater documentaries. Over the years, he was involved in more than 120 documentaries, wrote 50 books and set up an environmental foundation.
Year 3
The transition to Key Stage 2 begins in Year 3, and at Langley Academy Primary, we make sure that exploration, discovery, and curiosity-based learning methods continue to motivate our children to succeed in this constantly changing environment. This year, children will gain new skills and expand their knowledge in a diverse curriculum that includes lessons on the Victorians, dinosaurs, prehistoric Britain, France, Syrian refugees, and well-known campaigners, through engaging activities and trips to museums. The Year 3 work sample and other details on the class namesakes are provided below.
Mahatma Gandhi led non-violent protests to improve the lives of poor people in India. He encouraged people to protest peacefully to change things they didn’t believe was fair. His approach is summarised in this quote: “You must be the change you wish to see in the world.”
Nelson Mandela is now seen as an advocate for Human Rights, freedom and peace. He campaigned for equal rights and an end to apartheid. He is famous for being held in captivity for 27 years and then becoming South Africa’s first Black President. He considered education to be very important and this is summarised by: “Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.”
Rosa May Billinghurst was a British suffragette and Women’s right activist. As a child, she survived polio, but it left her unable to walk. She was an active member of the Women’s Liberal Federation and took part in many marches to fight for Women’s rights. At the time, the police would exploit her disability by capsizing her chair, or by letting the tyres down of her wheelchair. Once the government gave woman the right to vote, in 1918, she stopped her campaigning.
Year 4
The children continue to benefit from a stimulating curriculum created by Langley Academy Primary this year, with museum learning remaining at the core of all learning that takes place. The children use their own devices to promote our school's ethos by encouraging independent learning, enabling them to use digital technology to explore, discover, and be curious. Through trips to museums as well as digital resources, they will learn about the Romans, Ancient Egyptians, Japan, inspirational figures like Marcus Rashford, and the Vikings in fun and fascinating ways. Here are some details about our class names.
George Washington Carver was named after the first American President. He was born into slavery and was separated from his family at a young age. As he grew older, he became fascinated with plants and soils. He invented many uses for peanuts and sweet potatoes, ranging from soaps to paints. His inventions helped with the the production of crops and helped the poorer farmers improve the soil. He was the most prominent black scientist of the 20th Century.
Sir David Attenborough was born in 1926, the same year as the Queen! He was educated at the University of Leicester. Sir David is one of the leading environmentalists fighting for Climate change. He has been instrumental in raising the awareness of endangered species. He has over 10 plants and animals named after him.
Wangari Maathai was a Kenyan social, environmental and political activist. She was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize. She founded the Green belt Movement, in 1977, which focused on the planting of trees. She stood up against the former oppressive regime in Kenya, fighting for democracy.
Year 5
The Covid pandemic raised the profile of science. We have named the Year 5 classes after a range of scientists. We explore the perceptions of scientists through our unit on ‘Hidden Figures’.
Mae Carol Jemison is an American engineer, physician and NASA astronaut. She graduated from Stanford university with degrees in chemical engineering and African and African-American studies, before getting a medical degree from Cornell. She has worked for the Peace Corps in Africa as a Doctor. After which she became the first black woman to travel into space aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour. She has been included in both the National Woman’s Hall of Fame and the International Space Hall of fame.
Stephen William Hawking was the English theoretical physicist and writer. He was also the director of research and Professor of Mathematics at the University of Cambridge. He went to both Oxford and Cambridge University, where he got degrees and then a PhD in applied mathematics and theoretical physics. At the age of 22 he was diagnosed with form of motor neurone disease, which gradually paralysed him over the years, even to the extent of losing his speech. With the help of a speech-generating device, he continued his work and made serval large strides in the realm of physics. He also wrote a book ‘A Brief History of Time’ which was a best seller for a record breaking 237 weeks.
Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace was an English Mathematician and writer. She was the daughter to Lord Byron but became famous on her own merit. She is commonly referred to as one of the first computer programmers. She was the first to see the potential in using machines beyond pure calculation, and she wrote the algorithm to do this.
Year 6
By Year 6, we want our children to feel confident with who they are. We want them to have an understanding of their aims. Therefore, to prepare the children for their next stage of learning, classes are named after trailblazers. A range of people who have overcome adversity to fulfil their dreams. We know a bright future awaits out pupils.
David Bowie was one of the most influential writers and performers of popular music. He was also an art lover, actor and intellectual. He demonstrated a number of skills and talents. He did not follow traditional stereotypes of male performers. He was brave enough to represent himself in many ways. Bowie was able to show his musical range and creativity by releasing a wide range of songs over his 60 year career. He was innovative and visionary. His concepts managed to touch the hearts of many.
Malala Yousafzai is a human rights activist and advocate for female education. From the age of 11, she spoke out publicly against the ruling that prevented girls from being educated. After being injured in Pakistan, she came to England for treatment and has remained here ever since. She has received many awards. In 2014, she became the youngest person ever to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. She has founded a charity dedicated to giving all girls access to free, safe, quality education. She addressed the United Nations on her 16th birthday. She is also an author. Malala stands for integrity, courage, justice and inclusion. She is an inspiration. Her quote: “One child, one teacher, one book, one pen can change the world…” resonates with us at TLAP.
Kamala Harris became Vice President of the USA in 2021. She is the first woman and the first black woman to hold the post. Her parents are Jamaican and Indian. As an attorney, she has helped improve social justice. She is known for following her own views and not bowing down to pressure from those around her. She supports the empowerment of women. Harris reported her mother telling her, “Don’t just sit around and complain about things. Do something”. We want to encourage our pupils to be brave enough to challenge inequality and work to ensure they make a positive contribution to society, following their ‘moral compass’.
